crossRenderer.intent: Reveal or hide supporting content in place while preserving the surrounding context.

react: Uses button and region disclosure semantics with optional single or multiple open sections.
swiftUI: Uses DisclosureGroup with native indicator geometry, animation, and list integration.

crossRenderer.intent: Require an explicit decision before committing or abandoning a consequential action.

react: Uses an alertdialog portal with guarded outside and Escape dismissal plus explicit action and cancel controls.
swiftUI: Uses a native alert or confirmationDialog with platform button roles, ordering, and compact presentation.

alert.description: Faithful to prod @atom63/ui alert.tsx: a status callout with a default (neutral) variant plus four semantic tones. Visually, Alert is a static content/status surface; interactive controls only appear inside its action slot.

crossRenderer.intent: Communicate persistent semantic feedback and an optional recovery action.

react: Uses a web status-callout surface with composable slots.
swiftUI: Uses a compact native callout and avoids assertive announcements for persistent notices.

crossRenderer.intent: Represent a person or entity with an image and identity-preserving fallback.

react: Uses browser image loading and DOM fallback composition.
swiftUI: Uses native image decoding and SwiftUI loading phases.

badge.description: Solid/surface + semantic sets are faithful to prod @atom63/ui badge.tsx. Palette hues back category/tag colors via the `--a63-badge-*` contract in @atom63/styles (which references foundation --color-* primitives).

crossRenderer.intent: Communicate a compact label or semantic status alongside primary content.

react: May expose palette-only decorative variants outside the shared semantic subset.
swiftUI: Uses a compact capsule that expands for Dynamic Type.

button-group.description: Faithful to prod @atom63/ui button-group: horizontal|vertical orientation and the full text/icon size ramp. Sizes drive the welded control heights; the text sizes (xs..xl) size the text/label runs, the icon-* sizes make square icon-button runs. The DS recipe reads these off data-orientation / data-size.

crossRenderer.intent: Trigger a user-initiated action with explicit hierarchy and feedback.

react: Uses HTML button semantics with pointer and focus-visible feedback.
swiftUI: Uses SwiftUI Button with native touch and keyboard activation.

crossRenderer.intent: Select an allowed calendar date while understanding its day, month, and current selection.

react: Uses a visible calendar grid and may support single, multiple, or range selection.
swiftUI: Uses DatePicker with platform-owned compact, graphical, or field presentation and declared date bounds.

crossRenderer.intent: Group related content and optionally expose one primary action.

react: Hover and focus-visible may communicate interactivity.
swiftUI: Touch and keyboard feedback replace pointer-only hover affordances.

connected-panel.description: An in-flow disclosure whose trigger and expanded content share one continuous surface. It consumes trigger behavior for the header row and surface chrome for the panel itself; it is not an overlay because it remains in document flow.

crossRenderer.intent: Move to an internal destination or open an external destination while making that distinction explicit.

react: Uses a router-provided internal link and a protected new-tab anchor for external destinations.
swiftUI: Uses NavigationLink for typed in-app navigation and Link or openURL for external destinations.

crossRenderer.intent: Temporarily move the user into a focused modal task without losing the originating context.

react: Uses a compound modal dialog with a portal, focus containment, Escape dismissal, and trigger focus restoration.
swiftUI: Uses the native sheet presentation, adaptive detents, swipe dismissal, and a NavigationStack for modal task hierarchy.

crossRenderer.intent: Present a compact set of contextual actions or choices without navigating away from the current task.

react: Uses a focus-managed popup menu with keyboard navigation, checked items, submenus, and explicit destructive styling.
swiftUI: Uses native Menu with Button roles, Toggle or Picker choices, and platform-owned presentation and keyboard behavior.

empty.description: Empty is a composed low-emphasis state surface. EmptyMedia carries its only variant axis; EmptyErrorDetail adds a disclosure action inside that surface.

crossRenderer.intent: Explain absent or unavailable content and provide an appropriate recovery path.

react: Uses composable Empty slots for illustration, copy, and action.
swiftUI: Uses ContentUnavailableView while preserving recovery intent and hierarchy.

feedback-state.description: FeedbackState is a status pattern hosted by another surface. Its optional actions consume the action contract; the status media carries semantic tone.

crossRenderer.intent: Associate a control with its label, supporting description, and validation feedback.

react: Uses DOM label and description relationships.
swiftUI: Uses native Form layout and may reflow vertically for Dynamic Type.

frame.description: Faithful to prod @atom63/ui frame.tsx — an OS-style window/flyout chrome: an outer "tray" surface wrapping inner "panel" surfaces, with a shared border weight. Prod modeled this with `cva`; here the variant unions live in the foundation and the recipe keys off data-* attributes (badge/button pattern). Chrome is tray (outer) + panel (inner). `variant` is a named tray+panel PRESET; `tray` / `panel` override the preset surface; `border` is Frame-level (inherited by nested panels, per-panel overridable).

crossRenderer.intent: Capture a single-line text value with visible focus and validation state.

react: Uses HTML input behavior, browser autofill, and web focus chrome.
swiftUI: Uses TextField or SecureField with the native keyboard and autofill.
Adapts visual chrome when a grouped Form or sheet container owns the row surface without changing label, value, focus, disabled, or validation semantics.

item.description: Faithful to prod @atom63/ui item: the Item container has variant (default/outline/muted) + size (default/sm/xs); ItemMedia has its own variant (default/icon/image). The DS recipe reads these off data-variant / data-size.

crossRenderer.intent: Load the next collection segment and communicate recovery or completion.

react: IntersectionObserver may trigger loading while the explicit state renderer remains visible.
swiftUI: A list sentinel, task, or explicit load-more action may trigger loading.

crossRenderer.intent: Communicate an ongoing operation or measured completion.

react: May use a custom CSS indicator that follows web geometry.
swiftUI: Uses native ProgressView styles and platform progress animation.

crossRenderer.swiftUIRenderer: Picker(.inline) in a Form / AtomSelectionRow group
crossRenderer.intent: Choose exactly one value from a visible set of mutually exclusive options.

react: Uses radiogroup and radio semantics with circular indicators and keyboard movement.
swiftUI: Uses an inline Picker inside a Form or List, where each option is a row with the native selected trait (outside one, iOS draws a wheel), or grouped AtomSelectionRow controls.

crossRenderer.intent: Find or filter relevant content by editing a query without leaving the current collection.

react: Uses a labeled native search input with an explicit clear button and native form submission.
swiftUI: Uses searchable so placement, cancel, clear, suggestions, keyboard, and focus presentation follow the active Apple platform.

crossRenderer.intent: Switch a compact local mode or view between a small set of mutually exclusive options.

react: Uses a tab-backed segmented track with focus-visible feedback and an optional animated selection backplate.
swiftUI: Uses Picker with segmented style so geometry, typography, and selection feedback remain platform-native.

knownGaps.reason: Base UI Select moves DOM focus onto the options instead of keeping it on the combobox with aria-activedescendant, and has no option to change it. The APG Combobox pattern requires DOM focus to stay on the combobox (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/), so this is a gap, not a variant. Screen readers still announce the focused option.
Base UI Select 1.6.0 does not open the listbox on Home; only Enter, Space and the arrow keys open it. See docs/design-system/audits/base-ui-issue-drafts.md.
Base UI Select 1.6.0 does not open the listbox on End; only Enter, Space and the arrow keys open it. See docs/design-system/audits/base-ui-issue-drafts.md.
Base UI Select 1.6.0 treats Alt + Up Arrow as Up Arrow: it moves the highlight and keeps the listbox open. See docs/design-system/audits/base-ui-issue-drafts.md.
Base UI Select 1.6.0 closes the listbox on Tab without selecting the highlighted option. See docs/design-system/audits/base-ui-issue-drafts.md.

crossRenderer.intent: Choose one value from a finite set while keeping the current selection visible.

react: Uses web combobox and listbox semantics with keyboard highlighting, a positioned popup, and focus-visible feedback.
swiftUI: Uses native Picker presentation and platform-selected styles such as menu, navigation link, wheel, or segmented control.

separator.description: Faithful to prod @atom63/ui separator.tsx: a solid hairline (default) or a soft edge-to-edge gradient fade, in either orientation.

sidebar.description: Faithful to prod @atom63/ui sidebar.tsx: the Sidebar has three variant unions (side / variant / collapsible) plus the two menu-button ramps (variant + size) and the sub-button size ramp. The many structural parts each get a data-slot; these are enumerated as the contract's slots so consumers can target them.

crossRenderer.intent: Preserve layout while content loads without exposing placeholder content as real content.

react: Uses a CSS pseudo-element shimmer and media-query motion preference.
swiftUI: Uses a TimelineView gradient mask and environment motion preference.

crossRenderer.intent: Adjust a bounded numeric value through direct manipulation or assistive increment and decrement actions.

react: Supports horizontal or vertical orientation and optional multi-thumb ranges through web pointer and keyboard input.
swiftUI: Uses the native horizontal Slider with platform drag, keyboard, and accessibility-adjustable behavior.

crossRenderer.intent: Change a persistent boolean setting.

react: Uses web switch semantics with pointer and focus-visible feedback.
swiftUI: Uses native Toggle geometry and platform interaction feedback.

tabs.description: Faithful to prod @atom63/ui tabs.tsx: the TabsList carries a `variant` (default = a filled pill track, underline = an underline indicator, attached = borderless folder tabs) and a `size` ramp. TabsTab also takes the size so items scale with the list.

crossRenderer.intent: Switch between peer destinations or content views while keeping one selection active.

react: Uses tablist, tab, and tabpanel semantics with keyboard navigation and a visual indicator.
swiftUI: In-page sections use a segmented Picker above the content it selects, so each tab is a named, selectable button. TabView stays the renderer for app-level sections such as a tab bar or sidebar.

crossRenderer.intent: Capture a multi-line text value while preserving editing and validation semantics.

react: Uses native browser textarea scrolling and selection.
swiftUI: Uses TextEditor scrolling, selection, and keyboard behavior.
Adapts visual chrome when a grouped Form or sheet container owns the row surface without changing editing, focus, disabled, or validation semantics.

crossRenderer.intent: Announce transient feedback without interrupting the current task.

react: Portal placement follows the viewport and DOM stacking context.
swiftUI: Overlay placement follows safe areas and native transition composition.

crossRenderer.intent: Select or deselect a compact option without leaving the current context.

react: Uses a pressed-state web toggle with hover and focus-visible feedback.
swiftUI: Uses a touch-sized button-backed chip for compact filter selection.
